analysis:
Units examined: CHANGELOG.md (head text only, no patch), CONTRIBUTING.md (a one-line Go toolchain pin change, 1.25.0 to 1.25.7), deletion of coordinator/internal/store/cachemigrations/schema.go, and deletion of coordinator/internal/store/privacysql/logs.go (metadata only; no content supplied).

Security-relevant behavior: the CONTRIBUTING.md change is documentation only. Moving to a newer Go patch release is not a regression. The mise.toml pin and CI toolchain are not in this batch, so consistency between docs and actual pins is unverified.

schema.go deletion: it held DDL constants, DropChainHashDDL and BackfillColumnsDDL, for the cache_routing_holders table. They only dropped the anchor_chain_hash column and added measured_stage_ms, measured_expires_at and ready_boundary_mode. Dropping the chain hash is privacy-positive and relates to T-041 leak #2, but its removal is a legacy migration cleanup. The risk is that this file is deleted while callers still reference these constants, which would be a build break, or that the migration is no longer applied, leaving older tables with stale schema or the chain-hash column. I cannot see callers or other changes in this batch. The anchor_chain_hash column, if still present in deployed databases, would retain data the DDL was meant to purge. This is a residual data-retention question, not a demonstrated regression, and it is unverified.

privacysql/logs.go deletion: no content was provided, only removed-file metadata. Its name suggests privacy-related SQL for logs (T-051, T-058 relate to profiler tables and identity leakage in diagnostics). I cannot determine whether the removal drops a redaction or retention control or just moves it elsewhere. The next pass should check whether any privacy-sanitizing or retention logic was moved to a different package, and whether callers of privacysql still compile and apply the same protections.

No concrete security finding is supportable from the supplied evidence. needs_deeper_review is set because the deleted privacysql/logs.go content and the callers of both deleted files are not visible.
